item.title: Chinese peacekeepers to South Sudan (Wau) provide humanitarian assistance to local school
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
By Wang Yi, Gu Junjie, Gao Junwei, Zhang Zili, and Lu Yuyang Chinese peacekeepers pose for a group photo with the local students. (Photo by Gao Junwei) WAU, August 25 -- The 16th Chinese Peacekeeping Engineering Contingent to the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) in Wau recently visited a local girls' primary school to provide humanitarian assistance. Educational resources are scarce in the Wau mission area of South Sudan, where schools face inadequate teaching conditions and shortages of supplies for cultural and sports activities. The contingent carried out humanitarian assistance activities including Chinese language lessons, traditional Chinese cultural performances, and donations of supplies. School representatives expressed gratitude to the Chinese peacekeeping contingent for its assistance. The peacekeepers will continue to pay attention to the livelihood needs of nearby communities and carry out assistance activities to benefit the local residents.

item.title: China, India hold special representatives talks on boundary question in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 25 -- China and India on Tuesday held the 25th round of talks between the two countries' special representatives on the boundary question in Beijing, with the two sides engaging in comprehensive, in-depth, friendly and candid communication on the boundary question and bilateral relations, according to a statement released by the Chinese side. Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs and China's special representative on the boundary question between China and India, held talks with India's Special Representative and National Security Advisor Ajit Doval. Wang said China and India are important neighbors, as well as representatives of major developing countries and emerging economies. A healthy and stable development of China-India relations serves the fundamental interests of the two peoples, meets the common aspiration of countries of the Global South, and is in line with the trend of the times, Wang pointed out. Noting China-India relations have gone beyond the bilateral sphere and carry global and strategic significance, Wang said China is ready to work with India to view bilateral relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, strengthen communication, enhance mutual understanding, resolve differences and overcome obstacles, and be good neighbors and friendly partners that help each other achieve success, so as to realize "the dragon and the elephant dancing together." Wang noted that the two sides are orderly implementing the outcomes of the special representatives' meetings. Institutional exchanges and cooperation between the two countries are gradually resuming, while both sides are working together to maintain peace and tranquility in border areas. The two sides should draw lessons from history, place the boundary question in its appropriate position in bilateral relations, and continue moving forward without stagnation, regression or deviation, Wang added. Efforts should be made to gradually build a positive narrative on China-India boundary affairs and make dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation the mainstream, injecting positive factors into the healthy and stable development of bilateral relations, he said. Doval said China and India are both ancient civilizations, populous countries and important economies, and are partners rather than competitors. A stable, predictable and forward-looking India-China relationship serves the common interests of the two peoples and is of great significance to Asia and the world, Doval said. India is ready to further strengthen strategic communication with China, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, deepen multilateral coordination, effectively manage border areas, explore solutions to the boundary question and accelerate the improvement and development of India-China relations, Doval said. According to the statement, the two sides held in-depth communication on advancing boundary delimitation negotiations, strengthening border management, improving institutional mechanisms and promoting cross-border cooperation. They reiterated their commitment to seeking a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable package solution to the boundary question in accordance with the political guiding principles agreed upon in 2005, based on mutual respect and mutual understanding and through the special representatives' mechanism. The two sides will continue to properly handle the boundary question through dialogue and consultation and jointly maintain peace and tranquility in border areas. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of talks between the two countries' special representatives on the boundary question in India in 2027. The two sides also exchanged views on international and regional issues of common concern.

item.title: China warns against unilateral sanctions after U.S. vows "economic asphyxiation" of Iran
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
BEIJING, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- China has made clear on multiple occasions that it firmly opposes illegal unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and are not authorized by the UN Security Council, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said on Tuesday. Lin made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on media reports that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, expanding Washington's secondary sanctions threats and warning of dire consequences for countries that do not join the campaign. Economic warfare and maximum pressure do not help solve problems. Instead, they only escalate tensions and conflicts, create spillover risks, disrupt the global economic and financial order, and undermine the legitimate rights and interests of other countries, Lin said. The pressing priority now is to de-escalate the situation and return to the track of dialogue and negotiation as soon as possible, he added. China's cooperation with Iran is always conducted within the framework of international law and should not be disrupted or undermined, Lin said. China is closely following relevant developments and will take all necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests, he noted.

item.title: Xi puts forward four principles on Palestinian question
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping stressed on Monday that four principles should be followed to push for the resolution of the Palestinian question, which is at the heart of the Middle East issue. Xi made the remarks in talks with King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein in Beijing. First, a political settlement should be upheld. The two-state solution is the right direction, and efforts should be made to restart peace talks between Palestine and Israel, with a view to establishing an independent Palestinian state at an early date, Xi said. Second, the principle of "Palestinians governing Palestine" should be followed in advancing the governance of the West Bank and the post-war reconstruction of Gaza, he said. Third, humanitarian principles must be upheld. The international community, and the UN Security Council in particular, should shoulder its responsibility effectively to protect civilian safety, ensure the flow of humanitarian assistance, and put an end to humanitarian disasters, Xi said. Fourth, fairness and justice must be upheld. This means following international law, addressing both symptoms and root causes, and taking practical actions so that the Palestinian question can be resolved in a comprehensive, just and lasting way at an early date, he said.

item.title: Chinese FM calls on Middle East, Gulf parties to resume dialogue, negotiation
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, holds talks with Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kuwait, in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 24. 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei) BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday that the current situation in the Middle East and the Gulf region is once again at a critical juncture, expressing hope that the parties concerned will return to the track of dialogue and negotiation as soon as possible. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when holding talks with Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, minister of foreign affairs of Kuwait, in Beijing. Wang added the top priority is to de-escalate the situation. Wang said China always attaches great importance to its relations with Kuwait and stands ready to take the 55th anniversary of the establishment of bilateral ties as an opportunity to build a China-Kuwait strategic partnership with a more solid foundation, higher-quality outcomes and greater substance. Wang also expressed confidence that Kuwait will continue to support China's just position on issues concerning its core interests and ensure the safety of Chinese personnel, institutions and projects in Kuwait. Jarrah said Kuwait sincerely appreciates China's long-standing selfless assistance and support for Kuwait in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial integrity. Kuwait firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is ready to work with China to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state, Jarrah added. Jarrah noted that Kuwait stands ready to strengthen communication and coordination with China to promote the early restoration of security and stability in the Middle East and the Gulf region, and safeguard the freedom and safety of international waterways. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, holds talks with Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kuwait, in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 24. 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei)
